fatal_errors: The proposed zirconium-alloying intervention does not reconstruct the target intervention, which is optimization of low-temperature HVAF-i7 deposition of FeCoNiCrAl to produce a dense, minimally oxidized bond coat.
The cited evidence concerns Hf/HfC coatings and HfZr-gradient formation during hot-press sintering, not zirconium-doped HEA thermal-spray bond coats or thermal-barrier oxidation behavior.
The claimed Zr-enriched interfacial layer, oxygen-barrier function, and thermal-expansion-mismatch reduction are not established by the cited evidence.
The proposed approximately 900 °C cyclic salt-corrosion regime does not match the demonstrated 1000–1150 °C isothermal air-oxidation regime.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses durability of HEA bond coats and proposes a single, testable intervention, but it is scientifically disconnected from the hidden target. The target attributes improved oxidation resistance to an optimized HVAF-i7 process yielding 0.2% porosity, limited deposition oxidation, retained BCC structure, and a thin continuous alumina TGO. The generated hypothesis instead invokes Zr doping and a graded interfacial layer. Its untreated-composition control and quantitative spallation and adhesion measurements make the experiment reasonably discriminating, although the salt environment adds a corrosion mechanism absent from the target and the improvement thresholds are arbitrary. Most importantly, E1 does not support the proposed material system or oxidation mechanism, so this cannot qualify as a well-supported plausible alternative.
